title: Under the Yoke
author: Ivan Vazov
description: The classic Bulgarian novel, about a small town caught up in the failed April Uprising of 1876 against Ottoman rule. Vazov wrote much of it in exile and spent his last years in this house in Sofia.

title: Beyond Hitler’s Grasp
author: Michael Bar-Zohar
description: How Bulgaria’s 48,000 Jews escaped deportation in 1943, through the protests of politicians, priests, and ordinary people, including the deputy speaker of parliament Dimitar Peshev.

title: The Truth That Killed
author: Georgi Markov
description: Markov’s portraits of life under communism, first broadcast on the radio from London, about Sofia’s writers, party officials, and his own dealings with the leader Todor Zhivkov. Published after his murder.

title: Street Without a Name
author: Kapka Kassabova
description: A memoir of growing up in a concrete housing estate on the edge of communist Sofia in the 1970s and 1980s, and of going back years later to travel the country.

title: What Belongs to You
author: Garth Greenwell
description: An American teacher in Sofia falls into a fraught relationship with a young hustler he meets in the public restrooms beneath the National Palace of Culture. A novel about desire, shame, and a city.

title: Time Shelter
author: Georgi Gospodinov
description: A clinic recreates past decades for people with memory loss, until whole countries vote to live in the past. By a Sofia writer, it won the International Booker Prize in 2023.
